pages.title: Make the Dough
pages.text: First make a piece of $(thing)Wheat Dough$(): put wheat flour into a glass bowl of water.$(br2)Set the dough on the ground and right-click it with a $(thing)Kneading Stick$(); each hit has a 40%% chance to flatten it one stage, three stages in all, and every hit uses 1 durability.$(br2)Once it is as flat as it goes, right-click it with $(thing)Cheese$() and the dough becomes $(thing)pizza (unfinished)$().

pages.title: Kneading Stick
pages.text: Right-click the unfinished pizza with it to add one topping at a time, up to $(thing)five$(). Valid toppings include: butter, pumpkin, raw meat, raw fish, vegetables, sausages, plus cabbage, tomato, onion and so on.

pages.title: Cover With Cheese
pages.text: Once all five toppings are in, right-click once more with $(thing)Cheese$() and a $(thing)Raw Pizza$() drops out while the unfinished block disappears.$(br2)The raw pizza's tooltip lists every topping you chose.$(br2)It can also be placed down: it is a block, and breaking it returns the pizza with its toppings intact.

pages.title: Into the Oven
pages.text: Put the $(thing)Raw Pizza$() into an $(thing)Oven$() with the four slots loaded in order:$(li)Black Pepper Powder$(li)Sugar$(li)Black Pepper Powder$(li)Raw Pizza$(br2)The oven consumes all four ingredients at once and produces one whole $(thing)pizza$() block. The order matters — the pizza recipe matches by slot.

pages.title: Enjoy
pages.text: A pizza block holds $(thing)seven slices$(); right-click for one slice, and each slice restores hunger equal to $(thing)the total hunger of the five toppings ÷ 3$() with 0.3 saturation.$(br2)In other words, the heartier the toppings, the more filling the pizza.
